messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the PRD and prioritization for customer-managed networking by EOD tomorrow. Core asks from 3 pilot customers: BGP peering, stable egress IPs, DNS handoff, KMS-backed certs. Who can own launch gates?
Alex: I can own networking + BGP. Suggest we phase: Phase 1 = MVP (must-haves), Phase 2 = automation + UX, Phase 3 = polish (monitoring/rollouts).
Jordan: Sounds good. Need acceptance criteria and a test plan. Also define rollback criteria for config drifts.
Leo: Quick note re compliance/legal: handing static egress IPs may need contract language. Also propose SLA targets: control-plane handshake <500ms, route convergence <60s for customer routes.
Maya: Good call, Leo. Add that to risks. I'll compile a priority matrix (must/should/can) after we align on ACs.
infra-bot: RFC draft created: https://rfd.redwood/s/rfc-489 (edit access: eng-platform).
Alex: Draft priority matrix suggestion:
- MUST: BGP peering + basic route announce, assignable customer-egress-IP(s), TLS+mutual-auth for control channel, basic healthcheck & auto-failover.
- SHOULD: UI for egress allocation + status, automated BGP session provisioning, KMS integration for cert rotation.
- COULD: per-tenant traffic shaping, dynamic route filtering UI, onboarding wizard.
Jordan: Posting proposed Acceptance Criteria (please review):
```
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Customer can request and bind 1+ egress IPs per tenant via API.
- Control-plane TLS auth validated via CA chain; cert rotation tested.
- BGP session established; customer routes accepted and visible in routing table.
- Route propagation verified end-to-end to our edge and back to customer.
- Healthcheck: session down triggers automatic routing withdrawal and alert within 30s.
- Rollback: invalid config detected -> automatic rollback within 2 mins and incident created.
- KMS: key access flow validated for signing certs; rotation does not drop active sessions.
```
Leo: Edge cases we need to call out: overlapping customer subnets, NATed customer networks, asymmetric paths. Proposed mitigations: per-tenant SNAT pool, route prefix validation, and explicit customer opt-in for overlapping ranges.
Alex: Operational runbooks required: onboarding checklist, BGP debug playbook, emergency rollback steps, steps to reassign egress IPs without downtime. Add tickets: NET-502 (BGP core), NET-503 (egress allocation API), QA-520 (end-to-end test harness).
Jordan: I'll own the gating checklist and test matrix. High-level gating items: pilot w/ 2 customers (non-prod -> prod), smoke tests pass (connectivity, TLS, route visibility), no customer-impacting regressions for 48h.
Maya: Risks and blockers: legal for egress IP handout, capacity for reserved IP pools, cross-tenant leak risk, and automation gaps. We should mark legal sign-off and pilot completion as hard launch gates.
Leo: Also request metrics to monitor post-rollout: BGP session stability, route convergence time, control-plane latency, number of route flaps, and error rates. Set alerts on thresholds.
Alex: For implementation tradeoffs: do we rely on customer BGP, or offer an agent that tunnels routes? Customer BGP gives best performance but increases support surface. Agent-based route tunneling simplifies overlapping ranges but adds complexity to runtime. We should document both options in PRD and pick based on pilot feedback.
Maya: Action items: Alex -> scope MVP and owner for NET-502/NET-503; Jordan -> gating checklist + test matrix; Leo -> compile compliance/legal questions; I'll consolidate PRD and priority matrix then circulate. Sync 10:00am tomorrow to finalize owners and launch gates. :spiral_calendar: :thumbsup:
